title: DOING RIGHT WHEN NO ONE IS WATCHING

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now a priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father's flock. Some shepherds came along and drove them away, but Moses got up and came to their rescue and watered their flock." - Exodus 2:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses is a fugitive with nothing to gain. He is a stranger in a foreign land, and getting involved in a local dispute is the last thing a wanted man should do. Yet when he sees bullies driving away seven women, he gets up and helps.

Something has changed and something has not. The impulse to defend the weak is still there — that instinct was always from God. But this time there is no killing and no hiding. He simply stands up, drives off the shepherds, and then does the humble work of watering their flock.

Character is what you do when there is no reward and no audience. Nobody in Egypt would ever hear about this. He did it anyway.

And practically, this is how God gave him a home, a wife, and forty years of shepherding. Small acts of ordinary decency are often the doors God uses.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I help people when there is nothing in it for me?
2. Where can I stand up for someone weaker this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me the kind of person who helps when no one is watching. Give me courage to defend those who cannot defend themselves. Amen.
